title: Guided breathing exercise
description: A short breathing activity intended to help users practice slowing and steadying their breathing.
notes: General wellness activity; not a substitute for professional care.

title: Study planning activity
description: A simple activity for breaking schoolwork into smaller tasks and planning study time.
notes: Created by the project team; evaluate for clarity and usefulness.

title: Mental health information and self-care
description: Educational information about mental health and ways to care for emotional well-being.
notes: Review the specific page selected before presenting it to users.

title: Journaling and emotional reflection
description: A guided writing activity to help users describe feelings and reflect on what may be contributing to them.
notes: Optional activity; users should be free to skip prompts that feel uncomfortable.

title: Managing stress and everyday well-being
description: General information and practical ideas for supporting mental well-being.
notes: Check the selected guidance for audience and regional relevance.

title: Grounding exercise
description: A present-focused activity that invites users to notice details in their immediate surroundings.
notes: A general self-help activity, not an emergency intervention.

title: Workplace stress information
description: Information to help users explore work-related stress and possible support options.

title: Find mental health services
description: Information for locating mental health services and support in the United States.
notes: Support directory; availability and eligibility vary by location.

title: Peer support and recovery resources
description: Information about support options and resources for people seeking help with mental health or substance use concerns.
notes: Review individual services for suitability and availability.

title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
description: U.S. crisis support by call or text for people experiencing suicidal thoughts, emotional distress, or a mental health crisis.
notes: Keep in a separate safety pathway; do not trigger based on ordinary emotion labels alone. In immediate danger, call 911.
